prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a couple quick questions so I give the best, personalized guidance:
- When did the crash happen? (This affects deadlines.)
- How serious are your injuries and ongoing medical needs?
- Were you the driver, passenger, pedestrian, bicyclist, motorcycle rider, or hit by a commercial vehicle?
- Has any insurer already contacted you or offered money?
- Do you prefer a local Pleasanton/Alameda County lawyer or are you okay with a larger Bay‑Area firm?

While you answer, here’s practical guidance to help you choose the right lawyer.

1) What type of lawyer you need
- Look for a California personal injury attorney who handles motor vehicle collisions specifically (car accident attorneys). If a commercial vehicle, product defect, or catastrophic injury is involved, look for experience in those subareas.

2) Urgent steps (do these now if you haven’t)
- Get medical treatment and follow through with care—medical records link to damages.
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, damaged vehicle, witness contact info, repair estimates, police report number.
- Do not give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer or accept the first quick settlement offer before talking to a lawyer.
- Note deadline: generally 2 years from the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit in California (shorter rules apply if a government entity is involved—often 6 months to file a claim).

3) How to evaluate attorneys
Check for:
- Experience: years doing car-accident injury cases, number of cases tried to verdict, experience with similar injuries.
- Trial willingness: attorneys who only settle may accept lower offers; trial experience matters if insurer fights.
- Track record: settlements/verdicts in similar cases (not all firms publicize amounts, but ask).
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency fees range ~33% of recovery if settled before suit, higher if suit/filed. Ask about additional costs (litigation expenses) and who advances them.
- Communication: responsiveness, who on the team you’ll deal with, frequency of updates.
- Reputation and discipline: California State Bar records, client reviews (Avvo, Martindale, Google), Super Lawyers lists.
- Local knowledge: Alameda County/Pleasanton court experience and relationships with local experts (medical, accident reconstruction).

4) Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? How many?
- What is a realistic range of settlement for my case and why?
- What percentage of your cases go to trial?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- How do you charge (contingency %, expenses)? If we don’t win, who pays expenses?
- Can you provide references from recent clients?
- How long will this likely take?

5) Red flags
- Promises of a specific dollar amount before reviewing facts.
- Pressure to sign immediately.
- Poor communication in the consultation.
- No willingness to discuss trial experience.

6) Where to find and check attorneys
- California State Bar lawyer search (discipline status, bar admission).
- Local referrals: friends, family, your treating physician.
- Review sites: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google Reviews, Super Lawyers.
- Local bar associations: Alameda County Bar Association referral service.

7) What I can do next for you
- If you give details (when, injuries, insurer info), I can:
  - Suggest specific questions for your first calls.
  - Draft a short script/email you can use to contact attorneys.
  - If you want, I can compile a shortlist of well-reviewed Pleasanton/Alameda County personal injury lawyers for you to contact (you’ll need to tell me whether you want small/local vs larger firm).

Tell me the answers to the questions above or what you’d like me to do next and I’ll help you move forward.
